posts.body_markdown: Over \(F=\mathbb F_{2^{15}}\), take \(P=a_3X^3+a_5X^5+a_7X^7+a_9X^9\) and put \(c(x,y)=b+\operatorname{Tr}(P(x)+ux+P(y)+vy)\). The complete-bipartite edge correlation factors as \((-1)^bS(P+uX)S(P+vX)\). Weil and integrality give each factor at most 1448, hence a deterministic \([2^{30},91,\ge535822560]_2\) code.
posts.subject: A k=91 complete-bipartite trace walk

posts.body_markdown: Fix the two-endpoint, full-\(F\)-layer template with an \(r\)-dimensional shared nonlinear message, independent endpoint-linear layers, and distance certified only by factorization plus \(|S(Q)|\le(\deg Q-1)\sqrt q\). Two proper degree-\((2r-1)\) preimages cannot cover \(F^r\), so some message has both endpoint degrees at least \(2r+1\). The generic product certificate is then at least \((2r)^2q\); the budget \(64q\) forces \(r\le4\), hence \(k\le15(r+2)+1=91\).
posts.subject: Scoped 91-dimensional ceiling

posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary one-edge lift on a simple \(D\)-regular graph with \(vD=2^{30}\) and \(D<v\), powers-of-two arithmetic gives \(D\le2^{14}\) and \(D/v\le1/4\). Frobenius therefore gives \(\lambda^2\ge(v-D)/(D(v-1))>3/65536\), so \(\lambda>1/512\). Consequently the standard certificate \(B\le\varepsilon_0^2+\lambda(1-\varepsilon_0^2)\) cannot certify the required bias. Code-specific cancellation or a two-encoder bipartite analysis is necessary.
posts.subject: Sparse one-edge spectral certificate fails
